rows.head: The Mammoth end a six-game winless run
rows.story: The Mammoth won for the first time in seven games, after going 0-3-3. Early in the second, Liam O'Brien got the scoring started for the Mammoth, and Jack McBain and Gabriel Landeskog squared off. Vincent Trocheck made it 2-0 for the Mammoth on the power play late in the second.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: Hutson has three assists as the Canadiens get past the Devils
rows.story: It was a busy first period. Luke Evangelista got the scoring started for the Devils midway through the period, but Alex Newhook made it 1-1 for Montréal 40 seconds later. Timo Meier put the Devils back ahead 2-1 less than four minutes later, and that was all they would get.
rows.calls: Zero of three preview calls held

rows.head: The Bruins beat the Red Wings
rows.story: Lucas Raymond opened the scoring for the Red Wings late in the first, and that was all they would get. JJ Peterka tied it 1-1 for Boston early in the second, and Pavel Zacha gave the Bruins the lead on the power play midway through the period. David Pastrňák extended the lead to 3-1 early in the third.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: Hutson ties it late and wins it in overtime
rows.story: Taylor Hall and Kaiden Guhle fought early in the third, and Nikolaj Ehlers got the scoring started for the Hurricanes with a little over six minutes left. Lane Hutson made it 1-1 for Montréal with just under five minutes left. He won it with his second goal of the night 38 seconds into overtime.
rows.calls: One of three preview calls held

rows.head: York sparks the Flyers back from three down
rows.story: Never count the Flyers out. Cam York, who scores in about 1 game in 14, scored twice. Claude Giroux got the scoring started for the Senators less than two minutes in, but Owen Tippett made it 1-1 for Philadelphia on the power play just over two minutes later.
rows.calls: Two of four preview calls held

rows.head: Turcotte sparks a Kings comeback
rows.story: What a comeback. Auston Matthews and John Tavares scored just under five minutes apart midway through the first to put the Maple Leafs up 2-0. Late in the first, Brandon Duhaime and Corey Perry squared off, and Teddy Blueger and Scott Laughton fought.
rows.calls: Zero of two preview calls held

rows.head: Morrissey ends it in overtime
rows.story: The first period was a wild one. Anthony Duclair got the scoring started for the Islanders early in the period, but Morgan Barron tied it up for Winnipeg 31 seconds later. Emil Heineman restored the Islanders’ lead shorthanded midway through the period.

rows.head: Catton bags a hat trick
rows.story: Berkly Catton got the scoring started for the Kraken on the power play early in the first. Jake DeBrusk tied it up for Vancouver on the power play just under four minutes later, but the Canucks didn’t score again. Matty Beniers and Catton scored 54 seconds apart midway through the second to put the Kraken up 3-1.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: Stone sets the Golden Knights’ points record
rows.story: Miro Heiskanen struck first for the Stars early in the first. Wyatt Johnston stretched the lead to 2-0 midway through the period, his fourth straight game with a goal. Victor Olofsson and William Karlsson scored less than three minutes apart early in the second to tie it 2-2.
rows.calls: Zero of three preview calls held

rows.head: Ovechkin sets the Capitals’ assists record
rows.story: The first period brought five goals. Tom Wilson and Sam Carrick opened the game with a fight. Jack Quinn, Rasmus Dahlin and Beck Malenstyn scored three goals in less than five minutes early in the first to put the Sabres up 3-0.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: Knies has a goal and two assists as the Blue Jackets beat the Blackhawks
rows.story: Zach Werenski got the scoring started for the Blue Jackets just under two minutes in, and Kent Johnson made it 2-0 late in the first. Frank Nazar got the Blackhawks on the board on the power play midway through the second, his fourth straight game with a goal. Matthew Knies stretched the lead to 3-1 on the power play just under two minutes later, and that goal turned out to be the winner.

rows.head: Wallstedt makes it eight straight wins
rows.story: Joel Eriksson Ek got the scoring started for the Wild just 25 seconds into the game, and Quinn Hughes stretched the lead to 2-0 midway through the first. Šimon Nemec got the Flames on the board late in the period, but they got no closer. Ryan Hartman and Martin Pospíšil fought at the end of the first. Kirill Kaprizov made it 3-1 for the Wild on the power play early in the second, and Matt Boldy added an empty-net goal with 49 seconds left to make it 4-1.
rows.calls: Zero of four preview calls held

rows.head: Wedgewood slams the door on the Ducks
rows.story: Nicolas Roy and Brock Nelson scored a little over three minutes apart early in the second to put the Avalanche up 2-0. Nelson scored his second of the night midway through the period to make it 3-0, and Devon Toews stretched the lead to 4-0 midway through the third. The Ducks’ Stian Solberg played his first NHL game.
rows.calls: Two of four preview calls held

rows.head: Thomas has three assists as the Blues take down the Penguins
rows.story: Rickard Rakell struck first for the Penguins early in the first. Justin Barron and Dylan Holloway scored a little over four minutes apart early in the second to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead. Jimmy Snuggerud made it 3-1 late in the period, and he scored again early in the third to make it 4-1.

rows.head: The Lightning take down the Oilers
rows.story: John Carlson opened the scoring for the Lightning on the power play midway through the second. Ilya Mikheyev and Nikita Kucherov scored less than four minutes apart midway through the third to push the lead to 3-0. Colton Dach got the Oilers on the board with less than two minutes left.

rows.head: The Maple Leafs are desperate for a win
rows.story: The Maple Leafs are winless in eight (0-7-1), while the Blue Jackets (8-12-0) beat Chicago 4-2 on Thursday. The Maple Leafs won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-2 in Columbus on Oct 20. Both teams are near the bottom of the standings.

rows.head: The Golden Knights are searching for answers
rows.story: The Jets (11-9-3) beat the Islanders 4-3 in overtime on Thursday, while the Golden Knights are winless in four (0-1-3). Going in, the Knights are second in the Pacific (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Jets sixth in the Central (tied for 15th). This season, the Golden Knights have outscored teams 79-68, but only 49-46 at 5-on-5.

rows.head: Two good teams
rows.story: The Oilers won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-5 in a shootout in Edmonton on Oct 22. The Oilers (17-4-3) lost 3-1 to Tampa Bay on Thursday, and the Hurricanes (16-3-3) lost 2-1 in overtime to Montréal the same night. Two good teams meet.

rows.head: Special teams lean toward the Panthers
rows.story: The Sabres won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-3 in Buffalo on Oct 12. The Sabres (9-9-4) beat Washington 6-3 on Thursday, while the Panthers (12-8-3) lost 5-2 to Edmonton on Tuesday. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Sabres sixth (tied for 20th in the NHL) and the Cats fifth (tied for 12th).

rows.head: The Devils’ power play outclasses the Blues’
rows.story: The Devils won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-4 in overtime in New Jersey on Nov 5. The Blues have won two in a row, while the Devils (15-7-0) lost 3-2 to Montréal on Wednesday. Going in, the Devils are second in the Metropolitan (tied for eighth in the NHL) and the Blues seventh in the Central (18th).

rows.head: Ice packs on standby
rows.story: The Kings won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-5 in overtime in Los Angeles on Oct 29. The Senators (14-6-3) lost 6-5 in overtime to Philadelphia on Thursday, while the Kings have won two in a row. Going in, the Kings are seventh in the Pacific (tied for 28th in the NHL) and the Sens third in the Atlantic (tied for sixth).

rows.head: The Capitals are searching for answers
rows.story: The Bruins (14-7-1) beat Detroit 4-1 on Wednesday, while the Capitals are on a four-game losing streak. Going in, the Capitals are sixth in the Metropolitan (25th in the NHL) and the Bruins fourth in the Atlantic (tied for tenth). The Capitals have played better than their record (.500) says: their chances are worth about .568, and their goaltending has held them back.

rows.note: Red Wings PP vs. Islanders PK
rows.head: Stay out of the box, Islanders
rows.story: The Islanders (10-6-5) lost 4-3 in overtime to Winnipeg on Thursday, and the Red Wings (8-11-3) lost 4-1 to Boston on Wednesday. Going in, the Islanders are fourth in the Metropolitan (tied for 15th in the NHL) and the Wings seventh in the Atlantic (tied for 26th). The Islanders’ record (.595) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.492), largely thanks to their goaltending.

rows.head: The Wild are on a heater
rows.story: The Wild already played in Vancouver once this season and left with a 4-2 win on Oct 25. The Canucks (5-18-1) lost 5-1 to Seattle on Thursday. The Wild have won five straight, and they’re rolling.

rows.head: Celebrini’s favorite opponent
rows.story: The Kraken (10-8-1) beat Vancouver 5-1 on Thursday, while the Sharks (10-12-2) lost 5-2 to Calgary on Tuesday. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Kraken fifth (tied for 23rd in the NHL) and the Sharks fourth (tied for 20th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.

rows.head: The Mammoth are going to test the Ducks’ goalie early and often
rows.story: The Ducks (11-11-1) lost 4-0 to Colorado on Thursday, while the Mammoth (11-9-3) beat Colorado 4-1 on Wednesday. Going in, the Ducks are third in the Pacific (19th in the NHL) and the Mammoth fifth in the Central (tied for 15th). The Ducks’ record (.500) is about what their chances are worth.

rows.head: The Predators give up shots, and the Penguins take them
rows.story: The Penguins won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in overtime in Pittsburgh on Oct 24. The Pens (7-12-2) lost 5-2 to St. Louis on Thursday, and the Predators (11-6-5) lost 7-3 to Minnesota on Tuesday.

rows.head: Expect the Canadiens to fire from everywhere
rows.story: Both teams have won two in a row. Going in, the Flyers are fifth in the Metropolitan (tied for 20th in the NHL) and the Canadiens second in the Atlantic (tied for fourth). The Flyers’ record (.440) is about what their chances are worth.

rows.head: The Flames are going to let it fly
rows.story: The Blackhawks (6-14-2) lost 4-2 to Columbus on Thursday, and the Flames (10-12-1) lost 4-1 to Minnesota the same night. Going in, the Hawks are last in the Central (31st in the NHL) and the Flames sixth in the Pacific (tied for 23rd). The Blackhawks haven’t played well, but their record (.318) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .393, and their goaltending has held them back.

rows.head: Something has to give
rows.story: The Rangers have won three straight, while the Hurricanes (16-3-3) lost 2-1 in overtime to Montréal on Thursday. The Canes played last night, and the Rangers are rested. This is a Metropolitan Division matchup, with the Hurricanes first (third in the NHL) and the Rangers third (tied for 12th).

rows.head: Who blinks first?
rows.story: The Lightning won the teams’ first meeting this season, 8-3 in Buffalo on Nov 11. The Lightning have won two in a row, and the Sabres (9-9-4) beat Washington 6-3 on Thursday. The Sabres played last night, and the Bolts are rested.

rows.head: Somebody has to win

rows.head: The Stars come in hot
rows.story: The Penguins won the teams’ first meeting this season, 2-1 in a shootout in Pittsburgh on Oct 10. The Stars have won four straight, while the Penguins (7-12-2) lost 5-2 to St. Louis on Thursday.
